newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel hands down stiff sentences for stock fraud.
newsitem.headline: Israel hands down stiff sentences for stock fraud.

text.p: The Tel Aviv District Court on Thursday handed down the stiffest sentences in connection with stock manipulation in Israel's history, according to court documents.
The court found five former Israel Discount Bank employees and a businessman guilty of stock manipulation and fraud that took place over a couple of years in the early 1990s.
The sentences ranged from four to six years in prison and fines of up to four million shekels ($1.2 million). The six men had profited a total of five million shekels from the stock manipulation.
In handing down the sentences, the district court judge Amnon Strashnov said the men "had turned the stock market from an important institution into a national casino."
Israel Discount Bank, the country's third-largest, refused to comment on the sentences, noting that the five had been sacked when the scandal broke.

The stiffest sentence was handed down to the former director of investment services at the bank, who was given a six-year prison term, with an additional two-year suspended sentence and a four million shekel fine.
